doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Publishing: Harry Fox, BMI, his own company and business advice
summary: He explains Harry Fox, BMI and his own publishing company that gives an annual guarantee, and says Benny Golson and Gigi Gryce advised him that in jazz publishing just means ownership.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: By the way, how do you handle your, whats the publishing side that controls your music
Is that the Harry Fox thing?
Yeah. That's one of 'em. Uh, BMI is another one, Broadcasting Inc. Yeah. They uh …
Do you have your own publishing companies?
Yeah, of course. No, just one. Just … I have a publishing company, Bernita [?] Music.

Oh man, let me see. Quite a few years. And uh, one advantage of that is that every October, which happens to be now [chuckles], they give you a … if they can see uh to their uh whatever monitoring system they have that you, uh, uh, uh, your recording, your compositions, uh, are being recorded, either by you or by somebody else. They can see uh, uh, uh a loss, a down, a downward uh direction or upward direction in that. And accordingly, they give you what they call a guarantee once a year. And this is my month. So I smile every October. [chuckles]
Harry Fox collects for another part of your output.
Who else uh, gave you guidance as to what to do as a musician on the business side?

Oh well, Benny Golson, uh, the late Gigi Gryce, to a degree, and then uh, uh, I'm tryin' to think of some others, uh … uh, this is a constant discussion between uh me and musicians all the time, you know, how to uh manage your uh, uh, the ownership in the instrumental music simply means uh, as compared to uh, I mean uh, uh, if you have a publisher, if you publish uh, uh, uh a novel, for instance, uh, then uh you uh usually uh turn in a few chapters to the publisher and if they like it, they'll give you an advance to finish it. That's the concept I have of publishing a uh, uh, uh a book. But in uh instrumental music, jazz, that simply means ownership. You just own it. So uh it's a, it's a big uh difference, you know. You have to get it on the record which I was very fortunate, me and uh quite a few others uh were very fortunate early on to get uh these pieces that we'd uh composed uh onto recordings. And then uh the revenue can begin.
